Factors to Consider

Fox Corporation is expected to have entered the third quarter of fiscal 2026, benefiting from sustained momentum across its sports, news and streaming businesses, following solid fiscal second-quarter advertising and distribution growth. FOX Sports is expected to have remained a primary growth driver. The NFC Championship on FOX drew 46 million viewers in January 2026, reinforcing advertising demand. The Daytona 500 and continued college sports programming may have supported pricing trends. FOX Sports unveiled its FIFA World Cup 2026 broadcast schedule in January 2026, featuring 340 hours of live programming across 70 FOX network matches, expected to have accelerated upfront advertiser commitment activity. However, elevated sports rights amortization and production expenses may have continued pressuring profitability.

FOX News Media is expected to have maintained strong audience engagement and healthy advertising demand. Direct response and national advertising categories may have remained resilient, supported by strong scatter pricing trends and 200 new advertiser additions from the prior period.

Tubi's momentum is expected to have continued, with higher engagement levels and expanding younger demographics supporting digital advertising revenues. In February 2026, Red Seat Ventures, a Tubi Media Group division, acquired podcast platform Supercast, broadening its creator economy reach. FOX One is also expected to have contributed positively to distribution trends, continuing to gain meaningful traction among sports and news viewers.

title: James Murdoch Eyes $300 Million Vox Media Asset Deal
content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

James Murdoch could be preparing for a deeper push into premium media assets, with advanced talks underway to acquire New York magazine and several podcasts from Vox Media, according to people familiar with the discussions. His offer was approximately $300 million, one person said, though no deal is in place yet and another person said the assets could sell for much more. For investors, the potential transaction points to continued interest in recognizable media brands and podcast networks as audience attention becomes increasingly valuable across formats.

The discussions come after Murdoch, the youngest son of Australian media mogul Rupert Murdoch, cashed out the last of his share of the family's interest in News Corp. (NASDAQ:NWS) and Fox Corp. (NASDAQ:FOXA) last year through an agreement with his father and siblings. His private holding company, Lupa Systems, has already made several investments across media and pop-culture-linked businesses, including a streaming service in India and the parent company of the Art Basel fairs. Earlier this year, Murdoch also revealed plans to launch a new ideas expo in Switzerland, reinforcing a strategy that could possibly center on influential content, cultural platforms, and live-event-style media opportunities.

The podcast component may be one of the more important signals for the market. As listenership grows, podcasts have drawn interest from private equity firms and traditional media companies, while Netflix (NASDAQ:NFLX) recently began adding video podcasts to its streaming service. Vox Media's podcast network includes shows such as Pivot, Pretty Tough with Maria Sharapova and The Curiosity Shop, giving any buyer exposure to a format that could remain attractive as media companies look for loyal audiences and content that can move across platforms.

title: Electronic Arts Q4 Earnings Miss Estimates, Revenues Increase Y/Y
content:
Electronic Arts EA reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings of $1.59 per share, increasing 3.2% year over year but missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.25 by 29.3%.

Revenues increased 12% year over year to $2.12 billion and beat the consensus mark of $2.00 billion.

For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, EA’s net bookings were $1.86 billion, up 3.6% year over year. Management highlighted Battlefield 6’s record fiscal-year performance and noted Apex Legends delivered its strongest net bookings in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, alongside growth across Global Football properties.

Electronic Arts Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS SurpriseElectronic Arts Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Electronic Arts Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Electronic Arts Inc. Quote

Q4 Details of EA

EA’s full-game revenues (28.7% of total revenues) increased 39.4% year over year to $609 million. Full-game download revenues rose 43.9% year over year to $528 million. Packaged goods increased 15.7% year over year to $81 million.

Electronic Arts Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS SurpriseElectronic Arts Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Electronic Arts Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Electronic Arts Inc. Quote

Live services and other revenues (71.3% of total revenues) increased 3.6% year over year to $1.51 billion.

By platform, console revenues increased 9.4% year over year to $1.29 billion. PC & Other revenues jumped 30.3% to $555 million (from $426 million). Mobile revenues declined 5.2% to $272 million.

EA Expands Profit Despite Higher Operating Costs

EA’s cost discipline showed up in margins even as spending increased. GAAP gross profit increased 15% year over year to $1.76 billion. Gross margin expanded 220 basis points on a year-over-year basis to 82.8%.

Operating expenses increased 5.3% year over year to $1.19 billion. As a percentage of revenues, operating expenses contracted from 59.7% in the year-ago quarter to 56.2%. Research and development climbed to $732 million, while marketing and sales rose to $254 million.

Even with these increases, operating income on a GAAP basis improved to $564 million, increased 42.8% year over year, lifting the operating margin to 26.6%.

Electronic Arts' Balance Sheet & Cash Flow

As of March 31, 2026, EA had $2.98 billion in cash and short-term investments compared with $2.9 billion as of Dec. 31, 2025.

Net cash provided by operating activities was $580 million for the quarter and $2.55 billion for the trailing 12 months. Likewise, free cash flow was $519 million for the quarter and $2.32 billion for the trailing 12 months.

Deferred net revenues tied to online-enabled games rose to $2.23 billion, reflecting the company’s ongoing exposure to live services and digitally delivered content recognition timing.

EA declared a quarterly cash dividend of 19 cents per share, payable June 17, 2026, to shareholders of record as of May 27.

EA currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

American Public Education sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) at present, while Fox and Hasbro carry a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) each at present. You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

American Public Education is slated to announce first-quarter 2026 results on May 11. Meanwhile, Fox will report on May 11, while Hasbro is scheduled to release results on May 20.

title: Is It Too Late To Consider Fox (FOXA) After A 104% Three Year Return?
content:
Get insights on thousands of stocks from the global community of over 7 million individual investors at Simply Wall St.

For investors considering whether Fox at around US$62.23 still offers value or if the easy money has already been made, this breakdown is designed to help frame that question clearly. The stock has had a mixed recent run, with a 1.5% decline over the last week, a 6.2% gain over the last month, and returns of 26.8% over 1 year, 104.0% over 3 years, and 72.4% over 5 years, while being 15.6% lower year to date. Recent headlines around Fox have focused on the business as a core media player in the US, drawing attention to how its content assets and distribution reach position it within the broader sector. This context has kept investors focused on whether current expectations around its long term prospects are already reflected in the share price. Right now Fox scores 5 out of 6 on our valuation checks. This raises the question of how different valuation approaches compare, and whether there may be a more detailed way to think about what the stock could be worth by the end of this article.

Fox delivered 26.8% returns over the last year. See how this stacks up to the rest of the Media industry.

Approach 1: Fox Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) Analysis

A Discounted Cash Flow model takes estimates of a company’s future cash flows and discounts them back to today, aiming to show what those future dollars are worth in current terms.

For Fox, the latest twelve month free cash flow is about $2.33b. Analysts have provided forecasts for several years ahead, and these are extended further using a two stage Free Cash Flow to Equity framework. By 2030, projected free cash flow is $1.94b, with ten year projections ranging between roughly $1.32b and $2.56b before discounting. Simply Wall St then discounts each of these projected cash flows back to today using its model assumptions and sums them to arrive at an estimated equity value.

On this basis, the intrinsic value comes out at about $85.30 per share, compared with the current price around $62.23. That implies the stock is about 27.0% undervalued according to this DCF approach.

Result: UNDERVALUED

Approach 2: Fox Price vs Earnings

For a profitable company like Fox, the P/E ratio is a straightforward way to think about what investors are currently willing to pay for each dollar of earnings. Higher growth expectations or lower perceived risk usually justify a higher, or “richer,” P/E, while slower expected growth or higher risk tend to align with a lower, or “cheaper,” P/E.

Fox trades on a P/E of about 14.0x, which is close to the Media industry average of roughly 14.2x and below the peer group average of about 30.6x. On the surface, that suggests the stock is priced broadly in line with the wider industry and below some peers.

Simply Wall St’s Fair Ratio for Fox is 17.9x. This is a proprietary estimate of what the P/E might be given the company’s earnings profile, industry, profit margins, market cap and specific risk factors. Because it adjusts for these company level characteristics, it can be more tailored than a simple comparison with peer and industry averages. Comparing the Fair Ratio of 17.9x with the current P/E of 14.0x indicates the stock is trading below this model based reference point.

Narratives are introduced here as a simple way for you to write the story behind your numbers by linking your view on Fox’s future revenue, earnings and margins to a forecast, and then to a fair value that sits inside Simply Wall St’s Community page and updates automatically as new news or earnings arrive. This helps you compare that Fair Value to today’s share price and decide whether Fox looks closer to the cautious US$55 view, the optimistic US$90.37 view, or somewhere in between based on what you believe is more realistic.

For Fox however we will make it really easy for you with previews of two leading Fox Narratives:

Think of these as ready made storylines that connect the same set of facts to different conclusions about what the stock could be worth. Your job is to decide which feels closer to how you see the business, or to use them as guardrails for your own view.

🐂 Fox Bull Case

Fair value: US$71.00 per share

Implied discount to this fair value: about 12.4% compared with the recent price around US$62.23

Revenue growth assumption: 2.31% a year

Analysts in this camp see Fox holding revenue growth and margins broadly steady over the next few years, supported by demand for live news and sports plus steady advertising and affiliate income. The narrative leans on digital expansion at Tubi, pricing power in key events such as World Cup coverage and election cycles, and disciplined capital allocation across buybacks and investment. To line up with this view, you would need to be comfortable with Fox trading on a P/E above the current industry level in several years, with earnings and revenue reaching the consensus targets set out in the narrative.

🐻 Fox Bear Case

Implied premium to this fair value: about 13.1% compared with the recent price around US$62.23

The more cautious narrative puts weight on flat revenue, lower margins and the risk that higher sports rights costs and slower streaming progress keep a lid on earnings. This view assumes Fox may need to accept a lower P/E than the industry in a few years time, with earnings that are slightly below today despite ongoing share buybacks. Supporters of this narrative often point to the possibility that current expectations around advertising, distribution and digital growth prove too optimistic, which would pull fair value closer to the low end of analyst targets.

Put together, these two narratives bracket a range of fair values around US$55 to US$71, with the community split between those who think Fox is being priced too cautiously and those who see more downside risk if the tougher assumptions play out. The most useful next step is to decide which earnings path, margin profile and P/E level seems more reasonable to you, then anchor your own Fox valuation to that story rather than to the current share price alone.

title: First Phosphate shares surge as Agnico Eagle-backed Avenir moves into igneous phosphate
content:
First Phosphate shares surge as Agnico Eagle-backed Avenir moves into igneous phosphate Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Shares of First Phosphate Corp. (CSE:PHOS, OTCQX:FRSPF, FRA:KD0, OTC:FPHOY) closed nearly 18% higher on Tuesday after a landmark acquisition shook the North American igneous phosphate sector and drew fresh investor attention to the space.

The catalyst: Fox River Resources Corporation (CSE: FOX) announced it has entered into a definitive arrangement agreement under which Avenir Minerals Limited will acquire all outstanding common shares of Fox River for C$94.3 million in cash, which surpasses the full capital originally allocated to Avenir by its parent company, Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd (TSX:AEM).

Fox River holds a 100% interest in the Martison Phosphate Project in Ontario, a vertically integrated igneous phosphate operation designed to supply both domestic phosphate fertilizers and purified phosphoric acid for the lithium iron phosphate battery industry.

Avenir Minerals, established as an Agnico Eagle subsidiary in October 2025 to evaluate and advance critical and strategic mineral projects across Canada, had previously taken modest equity stakes of roughly 5% to 10% in junior miners spanning gold, nickel, zinc, antimony, and lithium. The Fox River transaction marks a significant departure from that strategy by acquiring an entire company in a sector where Agnico Eagle had not previously signaled interest.

With Fox River now off the board, igneous phosphate projects in North America have become a rare commodity. First Phosphate is among the few still standing. Its flagship Bégin-Lamarche deposit in Quebec has a 23-year mine life and is projected to produce 900,000 tonnes of phosphate concentrate and 380,000 tonnes of magnetite annually. A preliminary economic assessment assigns the project a pre-tax NPV of C$2.1 billion and IRR of 37.1%, with initial capex of C$675 million and a 2.6-year payback period.

In a critical minerals landscape where supply security is increasingly a strategic priority, this week's deal signals that igneous phosphate has arrived on the radar of the world's major mining companies.
